title: Constant-force work, kinetic and potential energy, work-energy theorem, and power

authority_basis.claim_scope: Current Grade 9 curriculum requires constant-force work, work-energy theorem, kinetic and raised-object potential energy, energy conversion, and power.
The engineering gate makes the required Grade 9 relations explicit with sign, geometry, unit, reference-level, and validity conditions without importing variable-force calculus.

concepts.statement: For a constant force acting through a displacement, work is the signed energy transfer associated with the component of force along the displacement.
concepts.why_required: It prevents treating the mere presence or magnitude of a force as sufficient for positive work.
concepts.failure_if_omitted: Perpendicular or opposing forces can be assigned positive work and energy changes can receive the wrong sign.

concepts.statement: Kinetic energy is the scalar energy associated with an object's motion and depends on mass and the square of speed.
concepts.why_required: The work-energy theorem relates net work to change in this state quantity.
concepts.failure_if_omitted: Work can be equated directly with speed or momentum without the required energy relation.

concepts.statement: Near Earth's surface, gravitational potential energy mgh is defined relative to a declared height reference under an approximately uniform gravitational field.
concepts.why_required: Potential-energy values depend on the chosen zero even though physically relevant changes remain consistent.
concepts.failure_if_omitted: Absolute potential-energy values can be compared across inconsistent height references or outside the near-Earth model.

concepts.statement: The net work done on the chosen object over a displacement equals the change in that object's kinetic energy.
concepts.why_required: It connects force-displacement reasoning with before-and-after motion states.
concepts.failure_if_omitted: A single force can be mistaken for net work or energy changes can be assigned without accounting for all forces doing work.

concepts.statement: Average power is the rate at which work is done or energy is transferred over an elapsed time interval.
concepts.why_required: It distinguishes amount of transferred energy from the rate of transfer.
concepts.failure_if_omitted: Equal work performed over different times can be incorrectly assigned equal power implications without considering duration.

Force and displacement refer to the same object and event
theta is the included angle between force and displacement
The same object mass and declared frame are used for the state being evaluated

model_conditions.condition: Use W = F s cos(theta) only when the force is constant over the displacement represented by s.
model_conditions.physical_reason: A changing force cannot in general be represented by one constant magnitude and angle over the whole path.
model_conditions.failure_consequence: The constant-force expression can return an incorrect work value for a variable-force path.

model_conditions.condition: Use U_g = mgh only over a height range where local g is adequately uniform and the height reference is declared.
model_conditions.physical_reason: The mgh relation is the near-Earth uniform-field form of gravitational potential-energy change.
model_conditions.failure_consequence: Potential-energy values can be applied outside their model or against an unstated zero reference.

model_conditions.condition: Work-energy theorem calculations must use the net work from all forces doing work on the same chosen object over the same displacement.
model_conditions.physical_reason: Delta K is determined by net work, not by an arbitrary single force contribution.
model_conditions.failure_consequence: A force contribution can be mistaken for the object's total kinetic-energy change.

representations.semantic_geometry: A common-axis diagram shows the chosen object displacement and the constant force vector with the included angle used to determine the force component along displacement.
forbidden_omissions: included angle or explicit parallel/opposite/perpendicular relation
must_not_imply: every nonzero force does positive work
a perpendicular force changes kinetic energy through work
representations.verification_method: Project the force onto displacement and check positive, zero, and negative-work limiting geometries before calculating magnitude.

representations.semantic_geometry: A before-and-after state table binds speed and height to K and U values using one declared frame and one potential-energy reference.
forbidden_omissions: height-zero reference when U_g is used
must_not_imply: potential energy has an absolute zero independent of reference
representations.verification_method: Check units and recompute state energies from the bound mass, speed, local g, and declared height reference.

reasoning_sequence.expert_action: Identify the object or system being analysed, the initial/final event states, and the displacement over which work is evaluated.
reasoning_sequence.failure_if_skipped: Forces, displacement, and energy states from different objects or intervals can be mixed.

reasoning_sequence.expert_action: Determine the force-displacement geometry and signed work contribution before using a work expression.
reasoning_sequence.failure_if_skipped: Positive, negative, and zero work can be confused.

reasoning_sequence.expert_action: Choose kinetic, potential, work-energy, or average-power relation only after its state and model conditions are identified.
reasoning_sequence.failure_if_skipped: A memorised energy formula can be applied to the wrong state, interval, or physical model.

reasoning_sequence.expert_action: Verify energy/power dimensions, work sign, reference consistency, and limiting geometries before accepting the result.
reasoning_sequence.failure_if_skipped: Dimensionally or directionally impossible work and power results can survive calculation.

required_transformations.description: Translate a force-and-motion description into an explicit force-displacement geometry before calculating work.
Translate before/after state data into the applicable kinetic, potential, work-energy, or power relation with model conditions retained.

misconceptions.incorrect_model: Any nonzero force acting on a moving object necessarily does positive work.
misconceptions.why_plausible: Force magnitude is salient while its direction relative to displacement is ignored.
misconceptions.required_counterexample: A force perpendicular to displacement has cos(90 degrees)=0 and therefore does zero work in the constant-force model.
misconceptions.required_representation_repair: Draw force and displacement in one diagram with the included angle explicit.
misconceptions.required_technical_repair: Use the force component along displacement to determine signed work.
misconceptions.verification: Check theta=0, 90 degrees, and 180 degrees to obtain positive, zero, and negative work respectively.

misconceptions.incorrect_model: The work done by whichever force is named in a problem always equals the object's kinetic-energy change.
misconceptions.why_plausible: The phrase work-energy theorem can be remembered without the qualifier net work.
misconceptions.required_counterexample: Two forces can do work of opposite signs so one contribution alone differs from W_net and therefore from Delta K.
misconceptions.required_representation_repair: List all forces doing work on the same object and interval before summing their contributions.
misconceptions.required_technical_repair: Apply W_net = Delta K only after constructing the complete net-work account.
misconceptions.verification: Sum all work contributions and compare the result with K_f-K_i.

problem_families.name: Signed work and work-energy under a constant force
problem_families.first_technical_move: Fix the analysed object and draw the force-displacement geometry before evaluating any work contribution.
fatal_errors: using one force contribution as net work
using variable-force calculus in the Grade 9 gate

falsification_cases.authoring_defect: Remove the force-displacement sign/geometry invariant so nonzero force magnitude alone can be treated as positive work.
Remove the constant-force model condition while retaining W = F s cos(theta).
